post.caption: Frying a mussel ruined a giant pearl. In 1857, a man in New Jersey fried mussels from Notch Brook, and he bit into a pearl that weighed about 100 carats. The frying had destroyed its shine. Soon after, another man found a pink pearl in the same brook. It weighed 93 grains, and by most accounts Tiffany paid $1,500. It reached Empress Eugenie of France and became the Queen Pearl. People rushed in, and within months the brook had no mussels left. The craze spread to streams in other states over the next decades. In the 1890s, Tiffany's gem expert studied American pearls.
